question.text: How many of Europe's top 20 grocery retailers will have public shrimp welfare commitments before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of the following retailers that, before July 1, 2027, have announced and not retracted any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as the Shrimp Welfare Project's [Where Can I Purchase Humanely Farmed Shrimps?](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps):

* Ahold Delhaize
* Aldi
* Asda
* Auchan
* Carrefour
* Co-op
* E. Leclerc
* Edeka-Gruppe
* Intermarché
* J. Sainsbury's
* Jerónimo Martins
* Magnit
* Mercadona
* Metro AG
* Migros
* Rewe Group
* Schwarz Group
* Systeme U
* Tesco
* X5 Retail Group
question.fine_print:
A welfare commitment must have been announced at any point before July 1, 2027, including before this question opens, but need not have been implemented.   

In case of grocery retailer mergers, entities are still treated distinctly for purposes of this question. Thus, if two companies in the above list merge and the successor entity has a qualifying policy, then both slots count toward the 10 that are needed for a **Yes** resolution.

# Shrimp welfare commitments among Europe's top 20 grocers: research notes (as of 2026-11-12)

**Bottom line:** 8 of the 20 listed retailers clearly have public shrimp welfare commitments today. Lidl (Schwarz Group) and Carrefour have narrower ones, which probably count under the "any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments" wording, bringing the total to 10. Ahold Delhaize and Rewe are unclear cases. I found nothing for the other 8.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-02-16 (last update): The Shrimp Welfare Project page "Where Can I Purchase Humanely Farmed Shrimps?" lists 5 of the 20 named retailers with both electrical stunning and an end to eyestalk ablation: Asda, Co-op (UK), Sainsbury's, Tesco and Les Mousquetaires (the Intermarché group). It also lists Albert Heijn, a subsidiary of Ahold Delhaize. It names none of the other 15, and it is out of date: Aldi's April 2026 pledge is missing. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps)
- The criteria accept other credible sources, so press reports and company statements also count.

## 2. Current status
My tally of the 20 named retailers:
- **Clear commitments (8):**
  - UK: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Co-op
  - France: Intermarché, Auchan, Système U
  - Aldi: Aldi Süd's pledge covers all its markets worldwide; Aldi Nord has a separate commitment to end eyestalk ablation.
- **Partial commitments that likely count under "any... commitments" (2):**
  - Schwarz Group, through Lidl GB and Lidl France ending eyestalk ablation
  - Carrefour, which plans to end eyestalk ablation by 2027-2029
- **Unclear (2):**
  - Ahold Delhaize: only through its subsidiary Albert Heijn. I found nothing at group level or from Delhaize Belgium.
  - Rewe: in 2025 a spokesperson said Rewe "aims" to end eyestalk manipulation in its conventional supply chains "if possible by 2027". This is a soft, press-quoted aim, not a published policy.
- **Nothing found (8):** E.Leclerc (confirmed as having no commitment), Edeka (declined to comment), Jerónimo Martins, Magnit, Mercadona, Metro AG, Migros, X5.
- Unless resolvers read the criteria strictly, the count is roughly 10 already. A strict reading would require both practices, a group-level policy and appearance on the SWP list. That gives about 5 on the SWP list today, or 8 if verified Aldi, Auchan and U policies are added.
- Ambiguity: "Co-op" probably means the UK Co-op. Coop Switzerland was not checked.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Que Choisir reports:
  - Mousquetaires and Auchan stopped eyestalk ablation for own-brand shrimp in January 2026 and plan electrical stunning by 2030.
  - Lidl has ended ablation for own-brand shrimp. It has no stunning commitment but is taking part in an ASC slaughter trial.
  - U: ablation ban by end of 2027 at the latest, stunning by 2030.
  - Aldi: ablation ended by 2031, stunning by 2035.
  - Carrefour: ablation ended by 2029, no stunning commitment.
  - Leclerc: no commitment, declined to comment.
  
  [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-11-02: Vivre Demain, citing ICAW (an animal welfare charity campaigning on shrimp) and AFP, says Intermarché, U, Auchan and Aldi have "full" commitments. It describes Carrefour's as partial (working on stunning from 2027). [Vivre Demain](https://vivredemain.fr/2026/11/02/crevettes-elevage-icaw-enseignes-epedonculation/)
- 2026-10-16 to 18: ICAW published a report on French retailers urging Leclerc and others to commit. [Marine & Océans](https://marine-oceans.com/actualites/la-grande-distribution-appelee-a-sengager-contre-la-maltraitance-des-crevettes-delevage/); [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/crevettes-cout-engagement-rse-distributeurs-2026)
- 2026-04-09: Aldi Süd committed worldwide (Europe, US, Australia) to end eyestalk ablation by 2030 and electrically stun all farmed shrimp by 2035, with annual progress reports. With this, all 11 major UK supermarkets have time-bound commitments. [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/04/09/aldi-sud-joins-other-major-uk-supermarkets-with-shrimp-stunning-commitment/); [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/with-aldi-sud-pledge-all-11-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-shrimp-welfare-targets/)
- Early 2026: Lidl GB says it ended eyestalk ablation in its core own-brand prawns from January 2026 and will introduce electrical stunning by end of 2026 (GB only). [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/lidl-gb-bans-eyestalk-ablation-for-farmed-prawns-joining-nine-other-u-k-retailers/); [Fish Farmer](https://www.fishfarmermagazine.com/news/lidl-move-on-shrimp-welfare-leaves-only-one-uk-supermarket-giant-without-a-timeline-for-change)
- 2025 (undated): Rewe said all its organic shrimp are free of eyestalk manipulation, with conventional supply chains targeted "if possible by 2027". Aldi Nord said it would end ablation by 2030/2031. Edeka gave no comment. [leinetal24](https://www.leinetal24.de/verbraucher/tierschuetzer-decken-grausame-garnelen-praktiken-auf-rewe-und-aldi-reagieren-zr-93976824.html)

## 4. Base rates
- From about 2023 (Albert Heijn first, then Tesco in 2024) to November 2026, roughly 15 major retailers across the UK, France and the Netherlands made commitments. [Rethink Priorities](https://rethinkpriorities.org/research-area/estimating-the-number-of-shrimp-in-major-european-markets/)
- Retailers on this list that added commitments during 2026: Aldi, Lidl, Auchan, Mousquetaires and U (formalised or implemented), plus Carrefour. That is roughly 3 to 6 new names in about 10 months, depending on how earlier statements are dated.
- Campaign groups: ICAW covers France, UK, Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland and Belgium. Mercy For Animals covers the UK. Southern and Eastern Europe (Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit, X5) appear untargeted. I found no evidence of campaigns there.
- Seasonality: not applicable.
- Retractions: I found none.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Metaculus community forecast or any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question.
- None of the prediction market prices supplied with the brief is related to it.

## 6. Upcoming events before July 2027
- ICAW's ranking covers Germany and Switzerland, so its next update could pressure Edeka, Rewe, Lidl/Kaufland Germany, Migros and Metro. I could not extract the current ranking PDF. [ICAW ranking](https://www.shrimp-welfare-report.org)
- Pressure on Leclerc continues after the October 2026 ICAW/AFP coverage.
- Deadlines inside or near the window:
  - Lidl GB: stunning by end of 2026
  - U: ablation ban by end of 2027
  - Co-op: by 2027
  - Rewe: aim of 2027
  - Carrefour: stunning work from 2027
- Aldi Süd's stunning research finishes in 2028. Annual progress reports are due.
- The SWP page may be updated to add Aldi, Auchan, U and possibly Lidl and Carrefour. It was last updated in February 2026.

# Shrimp welfare commitments among Europe's top 20 grocers: research notes (as of 2026-11-12)

**Bottom line:** On a broad reading of "any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments", about 13 of the 20 listed retailers already appear to qualify. That count includes eyestalk-ablation-only pledges and commitments made by subsidiaries. The SWP resolution page names only 5 of the 20 (6 if you count Albert Heijn as Ahold Delhaize). Which reading the resolver uses matters more than any new pledge. The fine print says 10 are "needed for a Yes", so this question seems to have started as a yes/no question.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-02-16 (date the page was last updated): SWP's "Where Can I Purchase..." page lists 12 retailers that have committed to both electrical stunning and ablation-free sourcing. They are Tesco, M&S, Waitrose/JLP, Ocado, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Morrisons, Iceland, Asda, Albert Heijn, Jumbo and Les Mousquetaires. The ones on the question's list are Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Asda and Intermarché (through Les Mousquetaires). Albert Heijn belongs to Ahold Delhaize, but the page does not name the parent group. The page does not cover ablation-only pledges or continental pledges from 2026. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps)

## 2. Current status: very likely qualifying on a broad reading
Already announced and not found to be retracted:
- **Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op (UK), Asda, Intermarché/Les Mousquetaires:** listed by SWP (above).
- **Ahold Delhaize:** qualifies through Albert Heijn (SWP). I found no shrimp commitment from Delhaize Belgium or from the group itself. [search](https://media.aholddelhaize.com/sustainability/our-position-on-societal-and-environmental-topics/animal-welfare)
- **Aldi:** in April 2026 Aldi Süd made a global pledge to end ablation by 2030/31 and adopt electrical stunning by 2035. Aldi Nord plans to end ablation by 2029/2031. [The Grocer](https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/aldi-sets-prawn-welfare-commitments-across-global-markets/717485.article), [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/with-aldi-s-d-commitment-all-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-time-bound-shrimp-welfare-standards)
- **Schwarz Group (Lidl):** Lidl's own-brand farmed shrimp has been ablation-free since January 2026. Lidl GB has committed to electrical stunning for the UK. [Lidl](https://info.lidl/en/our-responsibility/acting-fairly/fish-seafood), [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/lidl-gb-bans-eyestalk-ablation-for-farmed-prawns-joining-nine-other-u-k-retailers/)
- **Auchan:** ablation dropped for own brands since January 2026; electrical stunning targeted by 2030. [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- **Système U:** ablation ban by end-2027 at the latest; stunning by 2030 (same source).
- **Carrefour:** aims to end ablation by 2029 for own and national brands. It says it will work on stunning "from 2027" but has made no firm commitment. [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/crevettes-cout-engagement-rse-distributeurs-2026)
- **Rewe Group:** ASC whiteleg shrimp to be ablation-free by 2030, black tiger by 2031. Organic shrimp is already ablation-free. [Rewe Group](https://www.rewe-group.com/en/wp-json/wp/v2/posts/19696)
- **Metro AG:** policy reported 2025-11-25. It requires pre-slaughter stunning of fish and crustaceans for own brands and asks shrimp suppliers to avoid ablation. [The Fish Site](https://thefishsite.com/articles/metro-introduces-new-stunning-requirements-for-seafood-supply-chain)

No commitment found:
- **E.Leclerc:** refuses to commit, according to ICAW and AFP (October 2026).
- **Edeka:** declined to comment in 2025; I found nothing newer.
- **Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Migros:** nothing found.
- **Magnit, X5:** I did not search these specifically and found no evidence of commitments.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Que Choisir published a table of French retailers' positions. Leclerc, Grand Frais and Picard have no commitment. [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-11-02: an NGO (ICAW) told retailers to stop ablation. [Vivre Demain](https://vivredemain.fr/2026/11/02/crevettes-elevage-icaw-enseignes-epedonculation/)
- 2026-10-16/19: ICAW's French report "Souffrance en Rayon" says about 50% of the French market has no full commitment and singles out Leclerc (22% market share). [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/crevettes-cout-engagement-rse-distributeurs-2026), [AFP via Boursedirect](https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/economie/la-grande-distribution-appelee-a-s-engager-contre-la-maltraitance-des-crevettes-d-elevage-afp-5e413eec44e188fc63d972a96ea7a81106a542fe)
- 2026-07: Rethink Priorities counts about 15-16 major retailers with shrimp commitments across the UK, France, Germany and the Netherlands. [RP](https://rethinkpriorities.org/research-area/estimating-the-number-of-shrimp-in-major-european-markets/)
- 2026-04: Aldi Süd's pledge means all 11 major UK supermarkets now have time-bound targets. [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/with-aldi-sud-pledge-all-11-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-shrimp-welfare-targets/)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- Rough cumulative count among the 20 listed retailers (my tally from the dates above):
  - Before 2024: about 0-1.
  - 2024: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda and Albert Heijn added.
  - 2025: Co-op (March), Les Mousquetaires (September), Rewe and Aldi Nord (autumn), Metro (November), followed by the French chains.
  - 2026: Lidl, Aldi Süd, Auchan, U and Carrefour.
- That works out to roughly 4-6 new retailers a year in 2025-26. The remaining holdouts (Leclerc, Edeka, Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Migros, Magnit, X5) are harder targets: they have refused, said nothing, or operate in markets where NGOs have little reach (Russia).
- Seasonality: not applicable.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Metaculus community forecast or any prediction market on this question. None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied relate to it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- ICAW is campaigning in France, the UK, the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland and Belgium. Leclerc and Edeka are the most likely next targets.
- SWP could update its resolution page, which was last updated in February 2026. That would matter if the resolver relies mainly on SWP.
- Lidl has said it will take part in an industry stunning initiative, and Carrefour says stunning work starts "from 2027". Both could be firmed up.
- Biocoop expects new commitments in 2027, though Biocoop is not on the list.
- Retraction risk: no rollbacks found. ASC's new farm standard phases out ablation by 2029-2031, which supports retailers that tie their pledges to ASC.

**Key uncertainties for the forecaster:**
1. Whether pledges by subsidiaries or single countries count for the parent group: Albert Heijn for Ahold Delhaize, Lidl GB for Schwarz, Aldi Süd and Nord for "Aldi".
2. Whether ablation-only or soft pledges count: Carrefour, Rewe, Metro's "ask" to suppliers.
3. Whether "Co-op" means Co-op UK. The question's background implies it does.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 7.5 months. Forecasts close on 2027-06-30 and the question resolves around 2027-07-01.

(b) **Latest known value:**
- The SWP list was last updated in February 2026. It names 5 of the 20 retailers directly: Asda, Co-op, Sainsbury's, Tesco and Intermarché (through Les Mousquetaires). It also lists Albert Heijn, which would add Ahold Delhaize.
- Adding verified company policies and press reports as of November 2026 gives:
  - 8 clear commitments: the 5 above plus Aldi, Auchan and Système U.
  - Schwarz (through Lidl GB's ablation ban and stunning commitment) and Carrefour (ablation ended by 2029). Both likely count under "any commitments".
  - Ahold Delhaize (through Albert Heijn) and Rewe (a soft 2027 aim) as plausible additions.
- Under a lenient reading, the count is therefore about 10 to 12.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About 10 to 11 under a reasonable reading. The count would be about 6 to 8 if resolvers rely strictly on the SWP list and require group-level policies.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** About 3 to 6 retailers on this list added commitments in 2026. Over 7 months, perhaps 1 to 2 more could follow, most likely Rewe firming its aim, Edeka, Leclerc under ICAW and AFP pressure, Migros or Metro. That points to about 11 to 13.

(e) **Historical variation:** Over the past roughly 10 months, the count rose by about 3 to 6. Southern and Eastern European retailers (Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit, X5) have seen no campaigns and will very likely stay at zero.

(f) **Expectations of experts and markets:** There is no market on this question. Campaigners (ICAW, Mercy For Animals) are actively targeting Germany, Switzerland and Leclerc. No retractions have been seen.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Resolvers use only the SWP list and require group-level policies, so subsidiaries like Lidl GB and Albert Heijn don't count. The result would be about 6 to 7.
- **High:** The German retailers (Edeka, Rewe), Swiss Migros, Metro and Leclerc all commit after ICAW rankings, and the subsidiary reading is lenient. The result would be about 15 to 16.

- Adding other credible sources dated up to November 2026, the count is about 10 under a lenient reading: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Co-op, Intermarché, Auchan, Système U, Aldi, Schwarz/Lidl and Carrefour.
- Ahold Delhaize (through Albert Heijn) and Rewe (a soft 2027 aim) are borderline.
